## Accepted Article

::: {.output-list .editorial-list}
::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge status-accepted">Accepted</span></p>
<h3>Spatial Structure and Determinants of Global Top Biomedical Scientists' Mobility from an Urban Network Perspective</h3>

Role: First author. Accepted by *World Regional Studies*.

This article examines top biomedical scientists' mobility trajectories from an urban-network perspective, comparing education and employment stages and analysing city-level factors associated with mobility ties.

[Details](papers/urban-network-biomedical-mobility.html){.publication-link}

## Submitted Manuscripts

::: {.output-list .editorial-list}
::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge status-submitted">Submitted Manuscript</span></p>
<h3>Structure and Formation Mechanisms of the Intercity Mobility Network of Top Global Biomedical Scientists: A Dual Whole-Network and Ego-Network Perspective</h3>

Role: First author.

This manuscript links whole-network mobility structures with scientist-level mobility ego networks, examining how urban conditions, multidimensional proximity, platform histories, and prior mobility ties are associated with intercity mobility.

[Details](papers/whole-ego-mobility.html){.publication-link}
:::

::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge status-submitted">Submitted Manuscript</span></p>
<h3>Pre-move coauthor ties and the direction of scientific mobility: A city-level choice analysis of highly cited biomedical scientists</h3>

Role: First author.

This manuscript treats intercity employment moves as event-specific destination choices and compares selected cities with candidate alternatives. The estimates are interpreted as associations with destination choice, not causal effects or verified recruitment mechanisms.

[Details](papers/pre-move-coauthor-ties.html){.publication-link}
:::
:::

:::

## Master's Thesis

::: {.output-list .editorial-list}
::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge status-thesis">Master's Thesis</span></p>
<h3>Intercity Mobility Network of Top Global Biomedical Scientists: A Dual Perspective of Whole and Ego Networks</h3>

The thesis uses a 500-scientist, 1970-2023 longitudinal database to connect whole-network analysis, mobility ego networks, WERGM, GIS, and career-trajectory classification.
:::

::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge status-output">Selected Research Output</span></p>
<h3>Assessment of Urban Resilience Based on Nighttime Light Remote Sensing and Fisher's Information Method</h3>

Role: First author. This study uses VIIRS-DNB daily nighttime-light data and Fisher Information Light to evaluate short-term urban resilience during the COVID-19 shock.

[Details](papers/urban-resilience-nighttime-lights.html){.publication-link}
:::

::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge status-output">Selected Research Output</span></p>
<h3>Analysis of the Spatial-Temporal Evolution of the Global Trade Network in the Context of COVID-19</h3>

Role: First author. This study uses UN Comtrade data to analyse changes in directed weighted global commodity trade networks from 2019 to 2021.

[Details](papers/global-trade-network.html){.publication-link}
:::

## Research Software / Data Products

::: {.output-list .editorial-list}
::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge status-software">Research Software / Data Product</span></p>
<h3>Author-Institution-City Linkage Toolkit</h3>

A public Python toolkit supporting author-publication linkage, affiliation parsing, institution and city normalisation, synthetic fixtures, offline mock transport, quality audits, and tests for Scopus-derived research-data workflows. The public repository does not include restricted Scopus data.

[GitHub](https://github.com/Olivia-wr-research/author-institution-city-linkage){.publication-link}
